title: Run, Little Calf
prompt: A one-minute 3D cartoon comedy, asked for over two turns. Turn one: on a sunlit slope a little orange calf stands daydreaming when a palm-sized red bird dives past yelling 'Quick, look behind you!'; he turns to find a chopstick-thin white snake stood bolt upright and staring back, screams and bolts, tears through the woods, clears the creek in one leap and runs face-first into a tree. Nursing his nose among the falling leaves he wails; his father — a burly orange-brown bull with long curved horns, slow of speech and long past being surprised by his son — ambles over, hears 'I jumped the creek and hit the tree,' looks the now-bare tree up and down and wonders aloud whether the tree shouldn't be the one crying. The bird lands at their hooves, the father asks it where the boy's mother has got to, and father and son freeze mid-glance. Bright, saturated cartoon-CG 3D animation, colloquial Mandarin dialogue, landscape 16:9, native foley throughout, and the brief expressly forbids any lettering on screen. Turn two asks for the opposite: with the cut already rendered, add Chinese subtitles without re-rendering a single shot — so the dialogue already carried in the clips' own audio is transcribed and burned in, and only the composite is rebuilt.
